sourceType: Official Government of Punjab tourism website
note: Facts extracted below; prose summaries are written in our own words, not copied verbatim from the source.
about: Foothills-of-the-Shivalik district, between the Beas and Sutlej, bordering Himachal Pradesh. Known as 'Land of Saints' and 'City of Mangoes'. Famous worldwide for Sheesham Wood Inlay work and lacquerware, centered on Dabbi Bazaar.

places.name: Dholbaha Archaeological Site
places.facts: Evidence of Palaeolithic habitation, Indus Valley Civilisation, and a temple town (700-1200 AD); Hindu-Shahi style architecture introduced under Jaipal in 965 AD. Artefacts also held at the Hoshiarpur Archaeological Museum.

places.name: Archaeological Museum, Hoshiarpur
places.facts: Established 7 November 1971 by Vice President G.S. Pathak; houses prehistoric Dholbaha artefacts, fossils, sculptures.

places.name: Sheesh Mahal, Hoshiarpur
places.facts: Built 1911 by Lala Hans Raj Jain to mark a coronation ceremony; entirely glass-faced with sculptural decoration; functions as a Jain temple.

places.name: Bajwara Fort
places.facts: Heritage fort, listed among key cultural/heritage sites.

places.name: Gurdwara Sri Garna Sahib, Bodal
places.facts: Associated with Guru Hargobind Sahib Ji.

places.name: Kamahi Devi Temple
places.facts: Dedicated to Goddess Kamakshi, in the foothills terrain.

places.name: Takhni Rehmapur Wildlife Sanctuary
places.facts: Principal eco-tourism site in Shivalik foothills; nature walks, birdwatching, migratory birds.

places.name: Dabbi Bazaar (Inlay Work and Lacquerware Market)
places.facts: Principal market for Sheesham Wood Inlay work; Cottage Industries Corporation and shops like Gunesh Jain; Octagonal Well also here.

howToReach.air: Adampur Airport, Jalandhar (~30km); Shaheed Bhagat Singh International Airport, Chandigarh (Mohali)
howToReach.road: Bhagwan Valmiki Interstate Bus Terminal, Hoshiarpur

visitorInfo.bestTimeToVisit: February to April, September to November
